name: OpenAI
monetization: Sells ChatGPT subscriptions, API access, and enterprise AI; deeply loss-making at scale and funded by the largest private capital raises in history.
description_md: OpenAI is the developer of ChatGPT, the GPT model family, and Sora, and remains the densest node in the AI money graph: its compute commitments span Microsoft Azure, Oracle, AWS, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, AMD, and Broadcom. After the October 2025 recapitalization, Microsoft holds ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC; the company closed a $122B round at an $852B post-money valuation in March 2026 (Amazon $50B, Nvidia $30B, SoftBank $30B). It is also ~40% owner of the Stargate LLC data-center JV alongside SoftBank, Oracle, and MGX.
ai_monetization_md: Revenue is dominated by ChatGPT subscriptions (~$17B of the ~$25B annualized run rate at Feb 2026), with API consumption (~$6.5B) and Sora/licensing (~$1.5B) the rest. Full-year 2025 revenue was ~$13.1B against much larger losses — Microsoft's equity-method line implied a ~$11.5B quarterly loss in Q3 CY2025, and OpenAI projects a 2026 loss of ≥$14B. The business is a bet that scale and distribution convert into durable margin before the ~$600B+ of cloud/compute commitments (raised to ~$750B planned through 2030 per WSJ) come due.
ai_strategy_md: Lock up compute at unprecedented scale across every major cloud and chip vendor (Oracle ~$300B/5yr from 2027; Microsoft $250B Azure commit; AWS $38B plus a reported $100B expansion; CoreWeave ~$22.4B; AMD 6GW with a warrant kicker; Broadcom 10GW custom ASICs; Cerebras 750MW), diversify away from Microsoft after the April 2026 restructuring capped the 20% revenue share (~$38B through 2030) and ended exclusivity, and finance it all with mega-rounds (SoftBank >$60B cumulative, targeting ~13% by Oct 2026) plus early debt (BofA $520M bilateral line, $4.7B undrawn revolver) ahead of an IPO now pushed to 2027.
risk_notes_md: The central 'single point of failure' in the circularity debate: hundreds of billions of counterparty performance obligations (Zitron estimates ~$748B across Microsoft/Amazon/Oracle) rest on OpenAI revenue that is currently ~$25B annualized and loss-making (2026 projected loss ≥$14B). OpenAI missed internal targets in 2026 and pushed its IPO to 2027; several funders (SoftBank margin loans collateralized by its OpenAI stake; Nvidia's proposed ~$250B debt backstop) tie the ecosystem's credit quality to OpenAI's demand curve. Amazon's $50B investment is partly contingent ($35B on IPO/AGI milestones) — headline ≠ realized.

events.title: Closes $122B round at $852B post-money
events.why_it_matters: Largest private round ever; brings Amazon in as a major backer ($50B, $35B contingent) alongside Nvidia ($30B) and SoftBank ($30B), deepening investor-supplier circularity.

events.title: Microsoft partnership restructured: revenue share capped, exclusivity ended
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI's 20% revenue-share payments to Microsoft are capped (~$38B through 2030, ~$97B below the prior trajectory) and Microsoft's exclusive technology license ends; Microsoft retains ~27% ownership. Frees OpenAI to sell across all clouds but removes a structural Microsoft advantage.

events.title: IPO pushed to 2027 after missed internal targets
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI leaned toward delaying its IPO from September 2026 to 2027 amid missed internal targets and heavy spending commitments — a key date for the ~$35B contingent Amazon tranche and for SoftBank's leveraged position.
